commentary:
Energy owns the tape this morning. Brent punched through $100 for the first time since July after the US said it destroyed five Iranian tankers linked to the Revolutionary Guards following an attempted missile attack on a Navy warship, with Iran retaliating against a US base in Jordan — Brent is +2.6% at $100.48, WTI +2.1%, and the products are running harder still, heating oil +3.4% and gasoil +2.7% as cracks bounce. The curve is doing the talking: Brent's Dec-Dec spread closed at a record on a rolling basis and prompt backwardation widened sharply, signalling a genuine supply squeeze rather than a headline pop, reinforced by recovering Chinese crude buying.

TTF gas is up nearly 4% in sympathy. The transmission is straight into inflation and rates. The ECB is all but certain to hike Thursday, and the real debate is the terminal rate — bond markets are split, and much hinges on how long oil stays north of $100. Bunds, OATs and gilts are all lower, Euro Stoxx futures are off more than 1% with banks underperforming, and US index futures are soft as Treasuries slip at the belly. Any Fed easing hopes get harder to sustain with energy re-igniting headline CPI — India's inflation is already hitting 20-month highs on food and fuel.

Elsewhere, copper backed off its record (-0.9%) as Mideast risk weighs on growth-sensitive metals, while gold firmed on a softer dollar. The yen is bid after Treasury Secretary Bessent's "I am the house now" warning against shorting it post-intervention. Watch the ECB, US CPI, and whether Brent tests July's $102 high — from overbought territory.
